  September 30, 2021
  6:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL: At 6:03 p.m., on Thursday, September 30, 2021 the Alhambra City Council met in
Council Chambers and via video conference.

PRESENT via video conference:  MAZA, MALONEY, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ
PRESENT:  LEE
ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present physically and via video conference: City Attorney Montes, Assistant City
Manager Garcia, City Clerk Myles, Director of Community Development Ho, Principal Planner
Lam

CITY CLERK REPORT - NOTICE NO. N2M21-121

The City Clerk hereby reported that she duly gave notice of the special meeting of the City Council
being held this evening pursuant to the order of the Mayor and in accordance with Section 54956
of the Government Code of the State of California.

CONTINUED PUBLIC HEARING

1.  APPLICATIONS FOR VESTING TENTATIVE TRACT MAP TT 74194, RESIDENTIAL
  PLANNED DEVELOPMENT PERMIT RP-17-7, CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT CU-17-9
  AND DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE PROPOSED
  VILLAGES AT THE ALHAMBRA PROJECT (PROJECT) WITH 294 NEW, FOR-SALE,
  RESIDENTIAL DWELLING UNITS IN FIVE-STORY STACKED FLAT AND
  TOWNHOME CONFIGURATIONS; 545 NEW RENTAL APARTMENTS IN FIVE-STORY
  STACKED FLAT CONFIGURATIONS; AND UP TO 4,347 TOTAL PARKING SPACES
  TO ACCOMMODATE ALL NEW USES. IT IS EXPECTED THAT IF THE PROJECT IS
  APPROVED THE APPLICANT WILL IMPLEMENT A PARKING REDUCTION
  PURSUANT TO ALHAMBRA MUNICIPAL CODE SECTION 23.52.060. THE PROJECT
  SITE IS LOCATED IN THE PO (PROFESSIONAL OFFICE) ZONE. AN
  ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT REPORT HAS BEEN PREPARED FOR THE PROJECT
  AND WILL ALSO BE CONSIDERED WITH THE PROJECT ALONG WITH A POSSIBLE
  STATEMENT OF OVERRIDING CONSIDERATIONS – F2M17-50, N2M20-163

  Director of Community Development HO delivered a staff report. At the August 10, 2021
  Special City Council meeting, the Applicant requested a continuance to prepare an
  updated risk assessment for the project site. Following deliberation, the Council continued
  the meeting to this evening. On September 3rd, the Los Angeles Regional Water Quality
  Board approved an updated assessment work plan that would establish a new baseline
  for soil and soil vapor at key points, fill in perceived data gaps, conduct indoor air sampling

  1
9-30-21
   and evaluate lateral vapor migration from off-site sources, a copy of this assessment is a
  part of the September 30, 2021 staff report by the Director of Community Development.
  Additionally, at the time of the preparation of the September 30, 2021 staff report, the
  Applicant had not completed the updated risk assessment however, they intend to
  complete the work prior to September 30th. Any subsequent information received will be
  uploaded to the City’s website. Finally, an updated draft of the development agreement
  has been completed incorporating terms negotiated by the two Council Sub-Committees
  for Council’s consideration. Staff has reviewed the agreement and provided comments
  which have been incorporated into the agreement. The development agreement includes
  the following provisions: Inclusionary Housing; Vapor Mitigation; Hazardous Substances
  Indemnification (Corner Plan Area – Lot 8); Traffic Assessment and Management; Open
  Space and Community Access; Trees and Landscaping; and, Sales Tax Point of Sale
  Designation. Should the City Council provide direction to approve or deny the project, staff
  would return at a future meeting, as determined by the Council, with resolutions reflecting
  the Council direction. In that regard, also attached to the September 30, 2021 report by
  the Director of Community Development were excerpts from the City’s code concerning
  findings required for the entitlements requested for the project. Approval of the project
  would require the Council affirmatively make these required findings based upon
  information provided over the course of the Council’s various public hearings on the
  matter. Denial would require that the Council determine one or more of the required
  findings cannot be made, based upon information provided over the course of the public
  hearings. Should the Council direct preparation of approval documents, staff would also
  work with the Applicant on any revisions to the development agreement needed for clarity
  and implementation.

  Councilmember PÉREZ delivered a report from the Council’s Subcommittee. She stated
  that the Applicant worked with Equipoise Corporation and provided an update to their
  report and assessment. She also stated that the Council Subcommittee spoke with
  applicant, and as a result of study which found levels of pollution above initial expectations
  due to different formulas used in assessment, the applicant will provide mitigation of entire
  site.

  Appellant:  Megan MOLOUGHNEY, representing the Ratkovich Company, addressed
  the environmental concerns and explained the new report and explained that the
  attenuation policy was the only difference. She stated that they would install vapor barriers
  under all residential areas including the parcels that received closure with no deed
  restrictions. She stated that they were prepared to go above and beyond the required
  mitigation to ensure the development is safe.

  Rick BLACKMER and Chris STOKER of Equipoise Corporation, environmental
  consultants for the Appellant, provided a presentation regarding their Post Closure Vapor
  Intrusion Assessment Investigation performed in September 2021. The presentation is on
  file in the City Clerk’s office. Ms. MOLOUGHNEY reiterated that the Ratcovich Company
  voluntarily committed to additional sampling and agreed to install vapor barriers regardless
  of results. She went on to comment on the ways the Appellant met several requests from
  the Council.

RECESS & RECONVENE: Mayor Lee called for a brief recess at 10:24 p.m. and the meeting
resumed with all Councilmembers present at 10:36 p.m.

  Applicant comment:  Megan MOLOUGHNEY reiterated previous comments in
  support of the project approval.

  5
9-30-21
   Discussion: Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER thanked the public for their
  comments and noted that there seemed to be a resounding response. She thanked her
  fellow councilmembers, the Council subcommittee, and staff for their work to come up
  with the best project under many circumstances. She went on to state that the 2017
  environmental report was shown to be insufficient, that more testing was required, and
  that the site needed additional mitigation due to contamination levels found. She thanked
  the Ratkovich Company for the mitigation methods already implemented but noted that
  these were required to make the site safe. She went on to discuss the passive and active
  measures for mitigation. She noted that the only bright spot in the review of this project
  was the inclusion of a local workforce agreement. She stated that Council was proud of
  the agreement, but that the safety of workers could not be ensured during construction.
  Ms. Andrade-Stadler stated that there would be more opportunities to encourage unions
  with projects that would be more prepared for development. She stated that she wanted
  the workers to be safe and to provide projects where they would be able to live in the City.
  Ms. Andrade-Stadler motioned to deny the project, based on the adverse impact to public
  health and safety.

  Mayor LEE stated that she still had two remaining concerns with the project: the impact of
  traffic and circulation system performance on Fremont and the major intersections, and
  the remaining contamination of the site. She stated that the multiple traffic reports
  presented did not dissuade her concerns and that the latest environmental report made
  her other concerns greater. Ms. LEE and Mr. STOKER of Equipoise Corporation
  discussed the cancer risks for the entire site, the procedure and methodology used in the
  screening process and the assessment of risk, and the difference in the procedures used
  in 2016 and more recently. Ms. LEE went on to discuss the soil sampling and her concern
  that there were more contaminants deeper underground. She referred to Ms. Andrade-
  Stadler’s comments regarding passive and active measures of mitigation stating that soil
  removal was the best way to clean up the site. She stated that the project was not
  appropriate for residential use and expressed a wish that the site had been cleaned up
  prior to the application for development.

  Councilmember PÉREZ also thanked the public, the Council subcommittees, and Mr. Ron
  Sahu for his help in interpreting the technical reports. She thanked the Applicant for the
  further investigation and mitigation of the site; noting that all results and findings would
  continue to be used regardless of the current proposed project. She went on to discuss
  the negative public comments against Council, staff, the Applicant, and other residents
  and stated that Council was receptive to the public and valued the concerns. She
  acknowledged that the public hearing process could be improved and that Council’s
  deliberation could be conducted more efficiently. She again acknowledged the work of
  the Council subcommittees to assess the project and negotiate but added that
  unfortunately the project had not reached a point for the support of the community.

  Councilmember MAZA also thanked the public, staff, Council, and the Applicant. He went
  on to discuss the housing crisis, housing needs, pressure from the State on small cities
  via legislation such as SB9, the changes to R1 neighborhoods, and the need to find
  balance as a community to meet needs. He referred to the divisiveness during this process
  and made assurances that the Council had the best interests of the City at heart. Mr.
  MAZA, Mr. STOKER, and Mr. BLACKMER further discussed the reduced risks to
  contamination after the installation of the vapor barrier, the very low probability of lateral
  vapor mitigation from the development to adjacent properties, the ongoing process for
  testing, and the durability of the vapor barrier for 50 years. Mr. MAZA, Mr. BLACKMER,

  6
9-30-21
   and Ms. MOLOUGHNEY discussed the previous stages of the 3 remediation procedures
  conducted on the site between 2002 and 2011 including a soil vapor extraction system for
  deep ground, groundwater, and surface ground. Mr. BLACKMER confirmed that the data
  collected by multiple agencies during these processes, the screening levels and risk levels
  used met all criteria and that therefore there was no further remediation implemented on
  those parcels.

  Mr. MAZA and Ms. Renee PURDY, Executive Officer of the Los Angeles Regional Water
  Quality Control Board, discussed the site. Ms. PURDY stated that there had been
  significant investigation with updated and supplemented data, and that with institutional
  controls such as deed restrictions, soil management plans, vapor monitoring programs,
  and properly implemented engineering controls, that there would be public health
  protection for future land use at the site. She went on to discuss similar processes
  implemented at sites with similar conditions, stating that the site in question was not an
  uncommon situation. Mr. Hugh MARLEY, also representing the Los Angeles Regional
  Water Quality Control Board, confirmed Ms. Purdy’s statements.

  Mr. MAZA stated that there were still many concerns regarding the project such as density,
  traffic, affordability, and pollution on the site. He stated that the concerns with density and
  traffic were related to the number of units built which could be determined by Council. He
  went on to express concerns over future applications which might not require Council or
  Planning Commission approval under various state laws. He acknowledged the need to
  construct more affordable housing. He also acknowledged the need to attract responsible
  developers and development projects to improve areas in the City such as West Valley
  Boulevard.

  Councilmember MALONEY reiterated several comments made by fellow Councilmembers
  with regard to the housing crisis, scarcity of affordable housing, and the Regional Housing
  Needs Assessment goals for Alhambra. He stressed the need to communicate the loss of
  local control for housing development as context for Council’s consideration of this project.
  He also thanked the public, staff, and council for their efforts. He went on to acknowledge
  the Los Angeles Regional Water Quality Control Board and the Applicant for their work
  and efforts to change the initial project. He stated that this project was not the right one at
  this time. He stated that there were several changes in Alhambra since the project was
  first proposed such as an Inclusionary Housing Ordinance. He acknowledged the progress
  made through negotiations but added the lingering concerns of parking consistency,
  mobility and transit, affordable housing and soil vapors. He went on to assess the potential
  for future projects to be constructed without the consent of the City Council and outlined
  the multiple paths to new projects without the benefits of the negotiated points of this
  project. He expressed regret that an agreement could not have been reached with
  unanimous support.

  City Attorney MONTES and Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER reiterated her motion for staff to
  return with prepared documents for denial of the project, which was seconded by Ms. LEE.
  Mr. MAZA motioned to continue the public hearing at the regular City Council meeting on
  Monday, October 25, 2021 at 6:00 p.m., which was seconded by Ms. PÉREZ.

  Action Taken:  City Council directed staff to return with documents and
  resolutions at the regular City Council Meeting on October 25, 2021 to deny the project on
  the grounds that the project would have adverse impacts to health and safety.
